worldcombat.skill.speedswap.summary: Lock onto one living target in range (friend or foe) and exchange your movement speeds for a while: whoever was faster becomes slower until the window ends and both revert. Every living body shares one native movement-speed ruler, so the speed you gain is exactly the other side's real speed.
worldcombat.skill.speedswap.use.0: Borrow speed from a foe that outruns you
worldcombat.skill.speedswap.use.1: Lend your fast tempo to an ally that needs to catch up
worldcombat.skill.speedswap.use.2: Flip the order when a faster foe opens on you
Cast on one living target in range: the exchange holds %2$s within %1$s blocks and a clear line. Both revert to their original movement speed when the window ends or is cleared.
worldcombat.skill.speedswap.mode.exchang: Swap: the two effective movement speeds trade places — you gain everything if the foe is faster and lose everything if it is slower, symmetric risk; the window is longer (x1.15) and the cooldown is more expensive (x1.15).
worldcombat.skill.speedswap.mode.dampen: Dampen: both move toward the middle, halving the gap; steady and predictable, with a shorter window (x0.75) and cheaper cooldown (x0.85), but a slower foe drags you down.
worldcombat.skill.speedswap.timing: Cast on one living target in range: after %2$s of preparation it spends %4$s PP to swap; the recovery is %3$s, the cooldown %5$s from commit, and the current range %1$s blocks.
worldcombat.skill.speedswap.growth.0: At level %1$s the reach grows to %2$s blocks and the window lasts %3$s.
worldcombat.skill.speedswap.growth.1: At level %1$s the reach grows further to %2$s blocks and the window lasts %3$s.
worldcombat.skill.speedswap.preference.m: Swap: the two effective movement speeds trade places, symmetric risk, window x1.15. Dampen: both move toward the middle, halving the gap; steady, but a slower foe drags you down (window x0.75, cooldown x0.85).
worldcombat.skill.speedswap.preference.a: The partner only swaps while a threat or ally is this close; smaller keeps it for melee, larger chases out to flip the order.

The speed ratio (other / self) must reach this before the swap counts as worth it: borrow from a faster foe, lend to a slower ally. Higher keeps it for genuinely lopsided pairs and avoids pointless back-and-forth.
When on, the partner will also leave its post to swap speeds.
When on, allies that are clearly slower and need to catch up also become valid swap targets (lending them your tempo); off keeps the move for foes only.
world_combat.move.speedswap.text.fail: The target cannot take the swap
This move exchanges native movement speed, which decides how fast a body actually travels; other speed changes added during the window still apply, and only this instance's share is taken back when it ends. Equal speeds leave no window.
